title: The Last Oath Again
premise: Emrys Winterbourne, the last of the oath-bound swordspeakers sworn to speak truth into steel, has spent twenty years hiding in the Thornfell mountains since her order was purged. When a mute child arrives at her door speaking the First Tongue—the language that binds crowns to their wearers—Emrys learns that King Aldric is no longer human: something ancient has worn him for a decade, and it is hunting every speaker who could unmake it. Guided by the child Veyra and haunted by the ghost of her dead oathmaster, Emrys must gather the scattered fragments of her broken order's oath-blades, cross smuggler roads she swore never to walk again, and finally choose between the anonymity that kept her alive and the justice that gives her life meaning. In the end she speaks the Last Oath through her own blade at the cost of her swordspeech forever, freeing the king but binding herself, at last, to a people rather than a crown.
about_author: Wren Galloway is the pen name of a former trail guide who spent six seasons leading expeditions through mountain passes before turning to fiction full-time. Their work blends folkloric fantasy with quiet character studies, and The Last Oath Again is their third novel.

chapters.title: The Door in the Snow
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. A blizzard night; Emrys counts her stores and her scars, content in deliberate invisibility. A knock: a mud-caked child collapses on her threshold, murmuring syllables older than any kingdom. Emotional beat: the fragile peace of hiding shatters in a single heartbeat.

chapters.title: Words Before Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. She recognizes the child's language as the First Tongue, the speech her order used to bind oaths into blades—and into kings. Fear wars with duty. Emotional beat: dread awakening, the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: What the Child Carries
chapters.summary: Veyra POV, fragmented and dreamlike. Memories of a burning archive, a woman pressing a word into her palm, and a long flight north. Emotional beat: terror softened by the first safety she has known.

chapters.title: The Crown That Listens
chapters.summary: King Aldric POV. In the capital, the king wakes inside his own body for ninety seconds and understands he is a passenger. Something wearing his smile signs another execution order. Emotional beat: horror and helpless complicity.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. She weighs fleeing deeper into the mountains against the child's fevered nightmares, which show the capital burning. An old contact, Ferro the ferryman, sends warning: riders are asking after a girl. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: The First Blade Fragment
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Beneath her floorboards lies the hilt of her oathmaster's sword, one of seven fragments needed to speak the Unbinding. Touching it, she hears his ghost for the first time in years. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into purpose.

chapters.title: Riders on the Pass
chapters.summary: Ferro POV. Crown soldiers interrogate the ferryman; he lies badly, then well, buying Emrys three days at the cost of his own arrest. Emotional beat: ordinary courage in an extraordinary time.

chapters.title: Down the Thornfell Road
chapters.summary: Emrys and Veyra POV alternating. They descend the smugglers' paths Emrys knows blindfolded, teaching each other—she learns the First Tongue's cadence, Veyra learns survival. Emotional beat: wary trust becoming companionship.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot Her Name
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. In Lowmarket, someone recognizes her despite twenty years—a former apprentice, Sable, now a blacksmith who broke her own half-oath. Bitter reunion. Emotional beat: shame met with unexpected forgiveness.

chapters.title: Sable's Broken Oath
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Flashback to the purge: the order's massacre, the oath she abandoned to live. She refuses to join Emrys—but forges a scabbard for the fragment anyway. Emotional beat: guilt choosing small kindness over redemption.

chapters.title: The Wearing
chapters.summary: Aldric POV. The entity, called only the Regent, reveals it has worn eleven kings across nine centuries, consuming each realm's memory. It senses an Unbinding stirring. Emotional beat: cosmic menace made intimate.

chapters.title: Hunters in Grey
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The Regent's grey-cloaked speakers—corrupted survivors of the purge—ambush them at a shrine. Emrys kills for the first time in two decades and hates how easily it returns. Emotional beat: the cost of violence revisited.

chapters.title: Veyra Speaks
chapters.summary: Veyra POV. Cornered, the mute child screams her first word aloud in the First Tongue, shattering a hunter's blade. Her voice returns, but each spoken word ages her visibly. Emotional beat: power revealed as sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath the Lake
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Following Veyra's memories, they reach a drowned monastery where a second fragment rests beneath frozen water. Emrys dives; the lake remembers everyone who ever drowned there. Emotional beat: confronting the dead who demand remembrance.

chapters.title: The Oathmaster's Ghost
chapters.summary: Ghost POV, luminous and strange. Master Corvane admits he hid the child-lineage from Emrys, seeding her rescue of Veyra decades before her birth. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as faith.

chapters.title: Lowmarket Burns
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Retribution falls on the town for harboring them. Sable takes up her broken oath-blade mid-ruin and discovers the fragment in her forge sings when she holds it. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Three Fragments, Three Liars
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Sable joins them with the third fragment; the group dynamics fray as secrets surface—Emrys's role in the purge's failure, Sable's informer past. Emotional beat: found family built on confessed sins.

chapters.title: The Regent's Offer
chapters.summary: Aldric POV. The Regent, through the king's mouth, offers Emrys restoration of her order and pardon for all survivors—if she surrenders the child. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds of the King
chapters.summary: Aldric POV. During a rare lucid interval, Aldric leaves coded instructions in his private chapel for whoever comes to unbind him: do not save me if saving me costs the realm. Emotional beat: dignity within captivity.

chapters.title: Crossing the Weep
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The party crosses the Weeping Steppe, where the Regent's influence warps memory; travelers forget their names mid-stride. Veyra anchors them with First Tongue words. Emotional beat: identity tested literally.

chapters.title: What Emrys Forgot
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. In the Steppe's heart, Emrys loses her own name and must be told it back by Veyra. Stripped bare, she admits why she truly hid: not fear, but unworthiness. Emotional beat: the wound beneath the wound.

chapters.title: The Fourth and Fifth Fragments
chapters.summary: Sable POV. In a rebel-held quarry, surviving order members guard two fragments under a paranoid elder, Brannoc, who believes Emrys betrayed them all. Trial by testimony. Emotional beat: judgment by peers, verdict uncertain.

chapters.title: Brannoc's Verdict
chapters.summary: Brannoc POV. He condemns Emrys, but Veyra speaks a truth-word that forces his hidden memory open: he fled the purge himself, leaving children behind. Shamed, he yields the fragments. Emotional beat: hypocrisy unmasked, grace extended.

chapters.title: Six Blades, One Silence
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Six fragments assembled hum in harmony—but the seventh was melted into the royal regalia itself. The Unbinding must be spoken inside the throne room. Emotional beat: the plan crystallizes into near-suicide.

chapters.title: The Capital in Chains
chapters.summary: Veyra POV. They enter the city disguised as pilgrims; propaganda celebrates a king who has 'never aged.' Veyra sees crowds adoring their captor and rages at the seduction of comfortable lies. Emotional beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sable POV. To get weapons past the gates, Sable sells information to the Regent's hunters—a false trail, but a real betrayal in form. Emotional beat: moral compromise for tactical gain.

chapters.title: The Chapel Cipher
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Following Aldric's coded instructions, they find his hidden confession naming the Regent's true name and its one vulnerability: it cannot abide being named by an oath freely given. Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Grey Cloaks at the Gate
chapters.summary: Brannoc POV. The corrupted hunters catch up; Brannoc stays behind to hold the gate, dying so the others reach the palace. His last words forgive Emrys fully. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at the final price.

chapters.title: Throne Room of the Wearer
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. They breach the throne room; the Regent, wearing Aldric, greets them with perfect courtesy and offers Emrys her old life again. She refuses aloud, formally, in the First Tongue. Emotional beat: the refusal that starts everything.

chapters.title: The Regent Unmasked
chapters.summary: Aldric POV. Forced to witness, Aldric watches the entity shed his shape—a thing of borrowed centuries and eaten kingdoms. It seizes Veyra, the last vessel of the First Tongue. Emotional beat: abject despair before the turn.

chapters.title: Veyra's Choice
chapters.summary: Veyra POV. The Regent offers to restore all the years her speaking has burned away if she stops resisting. She answers with the truth-word that wounds it. Emotional beat: a child outwilling an ancient evil.

chapters.title: The Sixth Fragment Breaks
chapters.summary: Sable POV. Mid-battle, a fragment shatters; the Unbinding seems impossible. Sable realizes her forged scabbard, quenched in oath-memory, can serve as the seventh vessel. Emotional beat: ingenuity born of failure.

chapters.title: The Last Oath
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Climax. With Veyra's voice and Sable's scabbard, Emrys speaks the Unbinding through her own blade, offering her swordspeech as the freely-given price. The Regent is named, bound, and cast out of Aldric. Emotional beat: transcendence through total surrender.

chapters.title: After the Naming
chapters.summary: Aldric POV. Freed and aged ten years in a breath, Aldric faces his complicity. He kneels to Emrys publicly and abolishes the laws that destroyed her order. Emotional beat: accountability as beginning, not end.

chapters.title: The Empty Well
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. The price comes due: Emrys can no longer hear blades or speak oaths into steel. She mourns the loss like a death, then finds silence strangely clean. Emotional beat: grief and liberation entangled.

chapters.title: Trials and Testimonies
chapters.summary: Sable POV. The realm reckons with the purge; Sable testifies about her informer past and is pardoned but not praised. Justice outside law proves messier than vengeance. Emotional beat: honest, unsentimental repair.

chapters.title: What Veyra Keeps
chapters.summary: Veyra POV. Aldric offers Veyra a place at court as the tongue of treaties; she chooses instead to rebuild the drowned archive with Emrys. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: A School Above the Snowline
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. Months later, the mountain hold becomes a school for oath-speakers—not bound to any crown. Emrys teaches without powers, and finds that authority rooted in love outlasts authority rooted in magic. Emotional beat: legacy rebuilt on new terms.

chapters.title: The Visitor in Grey
chapters.summary: Emrys POV. A grey cloak arrives at the school—not a hunter, but a survivor seeking to lay down her blade. Emrys must decide whether the door that once saved her opens for the guilty. Emotional beat: mercy as the final test.

chapters.title: Oath Kept, Again
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, brief interludes. One year on: Aldric reigns mortal and accountable, Sable smiths blades that carry no bindings, Veyra archives a language reborn. On the doorstep, Emrys hangs a new sign: all who arrive are heard. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—justice as an ongoing practice.
